title: Fix shared load balancer conntrack namespace coalescing causing cross-tenant hostname exposure
creator: Ava Collins
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS lookups resolving to hostnames that belong to other tenants after a transient LB failover. Impact: hostnames and short-lived A records observed in telemetry implied cross-tenant exposure of internal hostnames. This ticket investigates the root cause and implements a production-safe fix to prevent conntrack/namespace coalescing across tenants on our shared load balancer layer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two tenants on the same Dedicated LB pool with VPC peering enabled
2) Create short-TTL internal hostnames (internal-svc.<tenant>.svc) and make high-frequency DNS queries from each tenant's pod during induced LB failover
3) Trigger LB failover by restarting the LB agent on node and flood connections to exercise conntrack entries
4) Observe DNS responses and conntrack mappings on the node (sudo conntrack -L | grep <ip>) and check if hostname meta leaks between tenant namespaces
root_cause: Our LB agent was reusing a shared conntrack namespace for accelerated datapath handoff when moving backend bindings between tenant pools. During rapid failover, conntrack entries for short-lived connection tuples remained and were re-associated with newly bound endpoints in a different tenant's network namespace, causing replies to be accepted and cached by the wrong tenant-side resolver. Combined with our overlay (Geneve) ARP caching and a coarse DNS caching layer, this allowed short-lived hostnames to appear in telemetry of the wrong tenant.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix deployed: LB agent now isolates conntrack tables per-tenant by using per-namespace conntrack sockets instead of reusing the global table (hotpatch rollout to LB pool 12, 14)
Added a short-lived aggressive conntrack flush on failover events (30s) while we backfill permanent fix
Temporarily increased DNS caching TTL enforcement to avoid accepting rebinds during failover windows for tenants with internal-only hostnames
design_decisions: Prefer per-tenant conntrack isolation at agent level rather than adding application-level workarounds (keeps kernel semantics consistent)
Avoid global conntrack table modifications that require disruptive kernel flags; implement user-space conntrack namespace creation and scoping in the agent
Do not change customer-visible default DNS TTLs as a long-term approach; only soften caching during failover windows
work_items: Agent: refactor LB agent conntrack code to create per-tenant conntrack handles and map to network namespaces (PR 2314)
Runtime: update overlay datapath to tag conntrack tuples with tenant-id where possible (compat shim for older kernels)
Control plane: expose failover hook to trigger controlled conntrack flush and DNS revalidation
Observability: add telemetry metric lb.conntrack_isolated and incident-level logs for cross-tenant conntrack hits
QA: run chaos job (chaos-lb-failover) against dedicated pools in staging for 72 hours
rollout_plan: 1) Staging validation: merge PR and run automated chaos tests in staging (48h)
2) Canary: rollout to 10% of LB pool capacity across two regions (US-West, EU-Central) and monitor metrics for 6h
3) Full rollout: expand to remaining pools with 15-minute pause windows and automated rollback on rise in cross-tenant-dns incidents
4) Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and final retrospective
tests: Unit tests for conntrack handle lifecycle and tenant scoping
Integration tests for LB agent failover that assert no cross-namespace conntrack entries are present
E2E chaos: repeated LB agent restarts + DNS churn asserting no cross-tenant hostname resolution seen in resolver logs
Performance benchmark: measure LB latency impact of per-tenant conntrack handles under 10k concurrent connections
qa_notes: In staging we observed a 1.8% increase in median LB CPU during high connection churn; acceptable within SLO. Need to validate under production-shaped traffic.
Edge case: kernels <5.4 lack conntrack-ns support; agent will fallback to per-process scoping with more aggressive flushes — document in release notes
